Flags are in tools/bencher/src/main.rs (RUSTFLAGS -C target-cpu=native) and Cargo.toml [profile.bench] lto = true, so A holds.

corrections.baseline: Protobuf (prost 0.14.4; Google's protobuf 4.36.1-release crate also on the page), FlatBuffers (flatbuffers 25.12.19), Cap'n Proto (capnp 0.27.0), MessagePack (rmp-serde 1.3.1); all are the Rust crates for those formats, not the C++ libraries
corrections.compiler_and_flags: rustc 1.100.0-nightly (a36d05efa 2026-09-09), LLVM 23.1.1; run as `cargo bench` by tools/bencher/src/main.rs with RUSTFLAGS="-C target-cpu=native", and Cargo.toml [profile.bench] sets lto = true (otherwise release-profile defaults, opt-level 3); criterion with default settings
corrections.hardware: AMD EPYC 9V74 80-Core Processor, 2 cores / 4 threads visible (Microsoft-hypervisor VM, GitHub-hosted ubuntu-latest runner per .github/workflows/bench.yml), x86_64
corrections.caveats: Numbers come from one dataset ('log') of a four-dataset suite (README last updated 2026-09-10). On 'mesh', flatbuffers serializes faster than bitcode (371.26 us vs 1.2265 ms). capnp and flatbuffers are zero-copy formats with no owned deserialize on the page. Their access time is in ns, so only serialize is directly comparable for them. The prost figures are encode-only and decode-only; they leave out populate and convert, which favors prost. Unlike protobuf, flatbuffers and capnp, bitcode is Rust-only and not self-describing. Its README also makes a stable format across major versions a non-goal. The run is on a shared 2-core CI VM built with target-cpu=native. Cargo.toml and README say MIT OR Apache-2.0, but the repo holds only LICENSE-MIT; the README's LICENSE-APACHE link points to a file that does not exist.

notes: Every quoted number matches the bitcode row and the baseline rows in the 'log' raw table: 96.821 us / 1.1452 ms / 703710 B; prost 731.23 us encode, 2.6802 ms decode, 884628 B; flatbuffers 763.63 us; capnp 480.15 us; rmp-serde 1.3179 ms / 2.3829 ms. The derived ratios are correct. Fixes: last_commit (2026-06-28 is the newest default-branch commit; 2026-06-29 was pushed_at), license (dual, per Cargo.toml and README), and flags (found in the harness).

The margin over capnp serialize on 'log' is small (~1.3x). capnp and flatbuffers are zero-copy formats with no owned deserialize on the page, so only serialize is comparable for them. The prost figures are encode-only and decode-only, which favors prost. The postcard README itself makes no speed claim; its design goals put memory and code size ahead of CPU time. GitHub's detector reports Apache-2.0, but the crate is dual MIT OR Apache-2.0, with both license files in the repo.

notes: All quoted numbers match the postcard row (366.95 us / 1.7399 ms) and the baseline rows in the 'log' raw table. The derived ratios check out: 2.0x, 2.1x, 1.3x and 3.6x for serialize; 1.5x and 1.4x for deserialize. Fixes: license set to the dual SPDX expression (per source/postcard/Cargo.toml and README), plus flags and hardware detail.
